newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sets unchanged Latin American banana quota.
newsitem.headline: EU sets unchanged Latin American banana quota.

text.p: European Union imports of Latin American so-called dollar bananas under a special tariff quota will remain at 2.55 million tonnes in 1997, European Commission officials said on Friday.
The quota, which applies to bananas grown on Latin American plantations owned by U.S. multinationals, was introduced in 1993 as part of the completion of the EU single market.

It was originally fixed at 2.2 million tonnes, but the EU's executive Commission later proposed an increase of 353,000 tonnes to cater for the needs of Austria, Sweden and Finland which joined in 1995.
For 1997, the Commission estimated imports of bananas from traditional African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) suppliers would total 700,000 tonnes, up 20,000 tonnes from last year.
Supplies from EU producers are expected to increase to 790,000 tonnes in 1997, an increase of 40,000 tonnes from 1996.
Overall EU banana consumption would be little changed at just over four million tonnes.

In May, the World Trade Organisation upheld a complaint by the U.S. that the EU import quota discriminatated against U.S. and Latin American suppliers in favour of the ACP countries, mainly former European colonies, which enjoy duty free access.
An EU appeal against the WTO ruling is due to be heard on July 11 with a possible decision in September.
